A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 41-page research work, including complete Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the version stamp and two stopping conditions in Algorithm 1.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original synthetic experiments, including empirical stopping times, comparisons with baseline algorithms, and APGAI failure counts.

after.justification: The same original experimental results remain in Section 6 and Appendix E, including Figures 1–2 and Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1's informal stopping rules are corrected: line 5 changes exploration termination from pulls 'not greater than' its budget to 'greater than'; line 9 changes exploitation termination from 'not smaller than' to 'greater than'. These are limited procedural corrections to the sketch. The detailed SEE algorithms, Algorithms 2–5, remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six synthetic scenarios: All Worse, Unique Qualified, One Quarter, Half Good, All Good, and Linear. Appendix E retains the same scenario definitions and APGAI evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain HDoC, LUCB_G, lilHDoC, adapted-TaS, and adapted-MS, including the omission of adapted-MS from All Worse. Appendix E.3 retains the separate APGAI evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain identical settings, including the arm counts, tolerance levels, mean rewards, main stopping cap of 10^8 pulls, and APGAI cap of 50000 times K. The sketch corrections do not establish a change to the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The qualified-arm-proportion analysis in Appendix E.2 and APGAI failure and stopping-time analysis in Appendix E.3 are unchanged. No ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains 1000 independent trials per setting and error bars described as three times the standard error. APGAI uncertainty reporting and the discussion of insufficient precision remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2, Tables 2–3, and their reported findings are identical. For example, APGAI's Unique-instance failure counts remain 373 at K=10 and 549 at K=50 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, lemmas, sample-complexity theorems, and proofs are unchanged, including Appendices A–D. The edits to the informal algorithm introduce no revised theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning SEE, near-optimal non-asymptotic sample complexity, and competitive numerical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the unresolved tightness with multiple qualified arms in Section 5.2 and the difficulty estimating APGAI's expected stopping time under forced truncation in Appendix E.3.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures in Section 4.2 and Appendices B.1 and E.1 remain unchanged, including SEE parameter schedules and the lilHDoC warm-up setting. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 3, Appendix A, and the references are unchanged. No cited works or substantive relationships to prior research are added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Language edits are confined to the two stopping-condition phrases in Algorithm 1 and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. The surrounding explanations, section organization, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2, Tables 1–3, algorithm-box structures, and page organization are retained. The local wording corrections do not redesign or relocate any display.

improvement.justification: Correcting Algorithm 1's reversed exploration-budget condition makes the informal sketch more faithful to the intended budget cap, while the exploitation edit agrees with Algorithm 4's loop boundary. This improves procedural clarity and accuracy. The detailed algorithms, proofs, and experimental evidence remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
